variants.candidate: Your judgment is only as good as the time you let it take in. Read one book slowly instead of five fast. Ask the oldest person you trust how they would do it, and hear them out to the end. Keep one evening a week with no one in it. Sleep on anything that costs money.
variants.original: Deep minds underrate their own output, so build the habit of releasing some. Once a month, teach one thing you learned to one person, because explaining it is how you find out it is really yours. Keep one notebook instead of six. And say your slow answer out loud before someone faster says a worse one.

variants.candidate: You get hardest on yourself when your strength has nothing to build. Give it something. Agree to one venture before you are sure. Put a date on the saving you keep putting off. Fix one thing at home with your own hands, and write the first line of the plan tonight.
variants.original: Growing things still need a gardener’s ruthlessness. Once a season, walk the whole field: feed what is fruiting, and let one dead project go without guilt. Keep the daily habits exactly as they are. And claim the growth out loud, raise the price, take the credit, sooner than feels polite.

variants.candidate: You keep being right in private, and that counts for nothing until someone hears it. Send the page before the third read. Tell a child one story with no lesson in it. Once a month, give something you made to someone who did not ask. Say the compliment the moment you think it.
variants.original: Ease is a gift right up until it dodges every hard thing. Pick one piece of what you make and finish it to done, not to pleasant. Say the awkward true sentence once a week, to the person it belongs to. Comfort that never risks anything eventually feeds no one.

variants.candidate: You do your best work when someone is allowed to tell you no. Pick one job this month that comes with a deadline and a judge, and ship it on time. Make the hard call out loud in front of the people it affects. Finish one small thing before anyone has to chase you for it.
variants.original: Fire that only knows battle starts inventing battles. Save your command for what deserves it: decide the small stuff instantly and cheaply. Build one boring routine that runs when nothing is burning. Peacetime is what the fighting was for, so practice standing in it.

variants.candidate: You treat rest as something you earn after the work instead of the thing the work runs on. Take rest in first and sleep before the hard decision rather than after it. Let one peer carry a job you could do yourself. Sit out one contest a month on purpose. Eat before you answer the message.
variants.original: Discipline that skips recovery is borrowing, and the interest is physical. Put maintenance on the calendar before it is needed: fixed bedtime, real meals, one full rest day a week. Track energy like money for one month. Treat the first sign of wear as a warning.
